correctness.rationale: For every m>=1 a leaf update followed by ordinary-clique updates gives an explicit route to the closed set. Inside it, hub and leaf cannot flip; ordinary transitions form exactly the two consecutive Boolean-lattice ranks. Each of the two resulting components is connected. The per-edge rate is exactly 1/(2m+2), and an up/down incidence commutator gives the entire Laplacian spectrum with smallest nonzero eigenvalue one. Direct full-state transition SCC checks m=1..4 and independent symbolic characteristic polynomial checks m=1..3 replayed successfully; finite tests do not replace proof. Boundaries and normalization are explicit.

originality.rationale: The published 2010 clique result has one recurrent class with the same total population. The change to a single-leaf odd clique disconnects this recurrent set into two equal-size classes and makes hub/leaf permanently frozen, a property not implied by the unperturbed clique statement. The known Johnson/middle-cube spectral algebra and equal-population binomial identity are excluded from novelty claims. Targeted literature and public result comparisons did not uncover a covering exact statement; historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: A single pendant leaf is a canonical local graph defect. In the established odd-clique stochastic-minority model, this perturbation freezes a designated spin and fragments one recurrent class into two without altering the total recurrent-state count. The result quantifies the entire spectrum and exact relaxation gap of the two surviving internally active components. This is a motivated all-size structural and dynamical contrast rather than a routine finite-count extension.
